responsibility.value: Provides a reusable generic CRUD base class (GetPagedAsync, GetByIdAsync, CreateAsync, UpdateAsync, DeleteAsync) for reference data entities, with abstract extension points that subclasses implement for mapping, search, ordering, and deletability checks.

Owns: Executing paginated read-only queries via ApplySearch → Order → ToPagedResultAsync pipeline with AsNoTracking
Fetching a single entity by Id with AsNoTracking and throwing NotFoundException if missing (GetByIdAsync)
Creating an entity via subclass-supplied factory (CreateEntity), persisting it via Add + SaveChangesAsync, and returning the mapped DTO post-save (so generated fields like Id/CreatedAt are populated)
Updating a tracked entity via subclass-supplied mutation (ApplyUpdate) then SaveChangesAsync — full replacement, not partial-field patch
Deleting an entity after a subclass-supplied deletability check (EnsureDeletableAsync, default no-op), then Remove + SaveChangesAsync
Exposing a protected IAppDbContext Db property for subclasses to access directly in their override implementations (e.g. EnsureDeletableAsync queries)
doesNotOwn: Authorization or access control — no authorization checks exist in the base class; relies entirely on the caller's controller-level [Authorize] attributes
Input validation — CreateEntity and ApplyUpdate receive raw TRequest as-is; subclasses do ad-hoc trimming but no null/format/length validation is enforced at the base level
Concurrency conflict detection — no row version or timestamp check exists; concurrent updates silently last-writer-wins
Cross-method transactional atomicity — each public method calls SaveChangesAsync independently; no ambient unit of work spans Create+Update or similar multi-call scenarios
Actual search logic — ApplySearch is abstract and fully delegated to subclasses; the base class only chains it into the pipeline

collaborators.detail: Injected via primary constructor and exposed as protected Db property; used for Set<TEntity>(), SaveChangesAsync(), and all EF Core operations
GetPagedAsync returns PagedResult<TDto> via the ToPagedResultAsync extension method
Implements the 5-method CRUD interface that defines the contract consumed by ReferenceCrudController
Generic constraint where TEntity : BaseEntity ensures the entity has an Id property used in all fetch predicates
Generic constraint where TSearch : BaseSearchObject ensures search properties (Page, PageSize, IncludeTotalCount) are available for pagination
Concrete implementation of IAppDbContext; the service calls Set<TEntity>(), SaveChangesAsync(), and internally the concrete context provides the actual EF Core pipeline

contracts: GetByIdAsync throws NotFoundException if no entity with the given Id exists in the database
GetPagedAsync returns a PagedResult with items ordered by the subclass's Order() method and filtered by the subclass's ApplySearch() method
CreateAsync persists a new entity and returns its mapped DTO with generated fields (Id, CreatedAt) populated from the database
UpdateAsync mutates an existing tracked entity via ApplyUpdate and persists the changes; throws NotFoundException if the entity does not exist

DeleteAsync removes an entity after EnsureDeletableAsync completes without throwing; throws NotFoundException if the entity does not exist; throws BusinessException if EnsureDeletableAsync detects referential integrity violations
assumptions: Caller enforces authorization at the controller layer — the service itself has zero access control, so reuse from a non-admin-gated endpoint would bypass all protection (no defense-in-depth)
No concurrent edits occur — no optimistic locking exists; two simultaneous update requests silently last-writer-wins with no conflict signal to the loser
TRequest properties are valid and non-null — no validation in the base class; a null string property causes NullReferenceException inside a subclass's Trim() call

Each CRUD call is an independent transaction boundary — callers needing atomic multi-step operations (e.g. create + update) must manage their own external transaction, as SaveChangesAsync is called inside each method
invariants: All query paths (GetPagedAsync, GetByIdAsync) use AsNoTracking — no unintended change tracking overhead on read operations
The NotFoundMessage is always a non-null string supplied by the subclass — thrown as NotFoundException(message) when an entity is not found
EnsureDeletableAsync always runs before Remove on the delete path — even if the subclass does not override it (default is no-op Task.CompletedTask)
failureModes: NullReferenceException in a subclass's CreateEntity/ApplyUpdate if the request carries a null property that is unconditionally Trim()'d (e.g. MusicStoreService line 14: request.StoreName.Trim() throws if StoreName is null)
Silent data loss on concurrent update (last-writer-wins) — the second SaveChangesAsync overwrites the first without any staleness detection

BusinessException thrown on delete if the entity is referenced elsewhere — EnsureDeletableAsync queries child tables (Instruments, MusicStoreEmployees, UserAccounts via IUserAccountService) and throws a human-readable message
NotFoundException thrown on any GetById/Update/Delete operation if the entity was deleted between fetch and the attempted operation (race condition, not guarded)
architecturalNotes: Real blast radius is MEDIUM, not high — exactly 3 concrete subclasses (MusicStoreService, InstrumentTypeService, AddressService), each consumed by exactly one admin-only controller (AdminMusicStoreController, AdminInstrumentTypeController, AdminAddressController). A bug here is contained to the Rentals → ReferenceData admin subdomain; no usage in academic, communication, or identity domains.
No optimistic concurrency control across all 5 mutation methods — this is the most impactful design gap given that admin users may concurrently manage reference data.
EnsureDeletableAsync pattern is well-designed: default no-op keeps simple entities (no children) simple, while entities with referential constraints override with specific child-table checks.
